title: Without saying who: impersonal and passive forms
description: Forms in -no and -to, the się construction and the passive with zostać.

blocks.text: Polish has several ways to leave out who does something. The forms ending in -no or -to describe a past action without a subject: zbudowano most (a bridge was built), otwarto sklep (a shop was opened). The się construction states general facts or rules: tu się nie pali (no smoking here), mówi się, że… (people say that…). The passive uses zostać for a completed event or być for a state, with a participle that agrees with the subject: most został zbudowany.

blocks.translation: A bridge was built here in 1990.

blocks.text: Mówi się, że to najlepsza restauracja w mieście.
blocks.translation: People say it is the best restaurant in town.
The shop is open until eight p.m.
blocks.note: Być with a participle describes a state.
